Aisha Khan: quick thread to capture follow-up from today's RFC sync — main ask: design a small, stable runtime negotiation for quant profiles that lets clients opt into aliases and lets infra steer traffic without breaking SDKs. tradeoffs: simplicity vs expressivity.

Ben Liu: summary of constraints i heard: 1) minimal per-request overhead, 2) stable wire headers for proxies, 3) ability to map deprecated profile ids to active aliases, 4) deterministic fallback ordering.

Clara Martinez: agree. proposal: profile alias table maintained in control plane, served to runtime as a compact manifest. runtime does a single lookup per request (profile_id -> active_alias), attaches header `X-Quant-Alias`, and uses precompiled kernels for alias. heavy calibration stays offline.

Fiona Zhao: what's in the manifest? sketch: `alias_id`, `primary_profile`, `fallbacks[]`, `quality_score` (offline), `compat_bits` (eg attn/kv cache flags). manifest should be versioned semver-like.

Gabe Rivera: prefer no per-request quality computation. Instead runtime exposes `quality_tag` (low/med/high) derived from offline calibration; clients can request higher quality via param `quant_quality_hint: high` which forces a different alias if available. example request: 

```json
{"model":"redwood-1","prompt":"...","quant_profile":"fp8-lite","quant_quality_hint":"high"}
```

Gabe Rivera: runtime then resolves alias and returns header `X-Quant-Alias: fp8-lite~qhi-v1`.

Clara Martinez: +1. also add an optional response body field `quant_resolution` that is small and nullable: `{ "alias":"...","applied_fallback":"int8-fallback-v1" }` so client SDKs can log and surface to devs. keep it opt-in via request header `X-Quant-Explain: 1`.

Ben Liu: we must be careful with older SDKs that assume the `quant_profile` field is authoritative. compatibility plan: 1) control plane serves alias mapping to runtime and also returns a `mapping_version` header; 2) for 60 days runtimes set header `X-Quant-Profile` (legacy) and `X-Quant-Alias` (new). after 60d we flip.

Aisha Khan: operational playbook notes: deploy manifest as config change with staged rollout. have canary with 1% traffic and a shadow path that logs `quality_tag` differences. if p95 latency regresses > 10% abort.

Fiona Zhao: how do we handle on-the-fly alias hotfix (eg patching fallback list)? manifest should allow hotpatching with a `hotfix` flag and require a two-phase commit: publish->runtime ack->promote. document in runbook.

Gabe Rivera: telemetry: emit `redwood.quant.alias.applied` counter + `redwood.quant.alias.quality_tag` histogram. tag by model, alias, customer_hash. default alert: >2% unexpected fallback rate for stable customers.

Clara Martinez: runtime impl note: alias resolution must be O(1) mem lookup and tolerates manifest staleness for up to 5m. use monotonic versioning to detect rollbacks.

Ben Liu: i'll own the control-plane manifest API + migration doc. Clara will own runtime shim. Fiona will draft runbook for hotfixes and staged rollout. Gabe will propose telemetry/alerts. Aisha will coordinate product/SDK changes.

deploy-bot: canary deployment `alias-manifest/v1.2.0` started id=1769997777.4 :rocket:

Aisha Khan: thanks all — next check-in tomorrow after canary logs. please add short PR links here when opened.
